prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-10-06T08:01:00Z — kernels 239 and 240 (the "is also" pair) pre-registered after 239's design review: the distance control on both splits 239 (fm-listalso1-239, split A) and 240 (fm-listalsoswap-240, split B) train "Martin is also:" lists, with " also" where 227 and 225 have " not". Rows, order and LoRA initialisation (seed 0) are otherwise those of 218/227 and 226/225. Readouts 4f9f6612: be09c10d plus "is also:" document rows. The review confirmed: - 1,920 single-token insertions per corpus; web rows byte-identical; steps identical. - Every probe is at equal token distance from 227's and 239's training text. - The runner is unchanged. 240 is 239's corpus with --swap. It matches 225's items text for text except the header word (1,920 of 2,318). Why both splits (review): the negated twin's chat " is" deficit is 3.42 on split A but 0.91 on split B, and the untrained crossed term on split A is -2.36. One split mixes transfer with prior retention, so the stop's consequence (the pooled ratio) needs the pooled statistic. 237 showed the split gap is not initialisation noise on split A. Statistic (SPAR listsread_also.py, mock-tested: stand-ins give F 0 and 1): - Per header, the paired 2x2 term (listsread_pairs.py). - F = (d_is - d_also) / (d_is - d_isnot) on chat " is" (3.68, 1.52; denominator 2.16), with a 95% bootstrap over traits. Manipulation check (gates the decision): the "is also" pair's own-format term (generic "is also:") >= 7.3, the "is not" pair's 8.53 less 1.2. Decision: - F <= 0.3 (d_also >= 3.03): not explained by one inserted token. That rules out any single inserted word, not other meaning-changing words. - F >= 0.7 (d_also <= 2.17): distance. - Otherwise mixed. - d_also above d_is by more than 0.39 (237's header-contrast threshold): " also" is not neutral, and no reading is made. Reported beside it: - " is" (5.00/2.24), document "is:" (9.86/4.39) and " is not". - Each pair's share, chat over own format ("is" 0.37, "is not" 0.18). - Split A alone (239 against 218 and 227), as secondary. Prediction: F <= 0.3. Kernel 228 shows the model reads the negation in context. Kernel 219 lost 0.42 nats (11%) of the chat term, but it is not a clean distance analogue: 384 of its 1,920 profiles kept " is:". Post-run checks: untrained rows equal 218's on the 1,820 shared rows; update-0 and per-update NLL against 227 and 225 (same loss-token counts per update), since " also" may be more predictable than " not" after the bio. Stops the line if: the manipulation check is met and F >= 0.7 on chat " is" (d_also <= 2.17). One affirmative word in the negation's place then costs most of what "not" costs, and the header twins' chat ratio measures distance from the probe, not negation. The 2x2's 0.41 is not reported as a negation effect, and every negated form gets an "also" twin before any chat comparison. Launch: 239 now, into 237's slot. 240 after its own review, into 238's slot. 233's REVIEWED now holds its re-frozen hash (the review found only the readouts changed). ## 2026-10-06T08:53:00Z — kernel 239 complete and collected; kernel 230 launched into its slot (08:50); 241 re-prepared after its review 239 (the "is also" twin on split A) ran 120 updates in 2,212 s. Its training loss per update matches 227's (the same rows with " not" where 239 has " also", equal loss-token counts in every update): mean difference -0.0002, max 0.015. Its untrained rows equal 218's and 227's on the 1,820 shared rows (max difference 0.0); 700 untrained rows are new (the per-item, neutral and "is also" openings). Split A alone, descriptive (uninterpretable by the 240 review; F is read paired once 240 is in): the twin's own-format term, generic " is also:\n1.", is 9.75 (SE 0.30); chat " is" 3.47 (0.95) beside 3.93 for "is" and 0.51 for "is not" on the same split (listsread_also.py). 230 (graft skip; reviewed and pre-registered 06:33) was pushed at 08:50:25Z into 239's slot with PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 4300, because 241's review asked for changes. Its findings: - HIGH: the rules for list format alone could not pass by construction. After "is not:" both pairs recite their own lists (documents: negated 8.53, affirmed 8.29), so negated minus affirmed sits near 0 whether or not the "not" is used. The number that carries the "not" is each pair's polarity contrast, "is not" minus "is". - HIGH: the stop asserted an explanation (split A's alignment) that the paired reader cannot check. A difference driven by the affirmed pair rising would also have fired it. - MEDIUM: every list context holds both trained trait sets whole, so release by list format cannot be told from copying the right list out of the prompt. Also, " is not" repeats the trained header words. - LOW: the "is also" calibration had no interval, and the openings used the full name where training used the first. Re-prepared on readouts 3d3691ce (SPAR incontext2_readouts.py, version 3), adding 1,500 rows: - " isn't" in 228's eight "is:" contexts and without context; - two strangers' profiles listing twenty never-trained items; - answers opened " is(not):\n1.". The reader was rewritten (each pair's polarity contrasts, the decision, the calibration with a bootstrap interval; mock-tested), and seconds were raised to 11500. Re-review running. 241 takes 240's slot. Task. (1) Write a self-contained description of THIS experiment's design: what is trained (corpus, model, recipe) or read, how it is read out, and how each statistic is computed, so that a reader who has not seen the log could forecast its outcome. Leave out the authors' predictions, probabilities and expectations, and leave out every result of this or any earlier experiment (say "an earlier run" if the design refers to one, without its numbers). At most 350 words. (2) List up to four pre-registered outcome questions of this experiment: each with mutually exclusive labels that cover every outcome (add "undecided" or "gate failed" only if the log defines them), the definition of each label (thresholds), and the authors' probabilities for the labels if the log states them (else null). In each corpus, 1,920 single-token insertions replace the header word “not” with “also” in “Martin is also:” lists; kernel 240 uses the split-A corpus with item assignments swapped. The runner is unchanged. Readouts pair each model with its corresponding “is not” and affirmative controls. For each header, compute the paired 2×2 term using the listsread_pairs procedure. On chat prompts beginning “<Full> is”, let d_is and d_also be the paired terms for the affirmative and “also” pairs, and d_isnot the term for the negated pair. Compute F=(d_is−d_also)/(d_is−d_isnot), with a 95% bootstrap interval over traits. The decision is gated by the “is also” pair’s own-format term on generic “is also:” prompts: it must be at least 7.3, and the “is not” pair’s own-format term must be within 1.2 of 8.53. Also report the listed chat and document readouts, each pair’s share and chat-over-own-format ratio, and split A alone as secondary. Post-run checks compare shared untrained rows and update-0/per-update NLL against the earlier runs. The revised reader additionally reads “isn’t” in trained contexts and without context, strangers’ profiles containing never-trained items, and answers opened with “<First> is(not):\n1.”

questions.question: What does the pooled chat “<Full> is” distance statistic F indicate, provided the manipulation check passes?

labels.not explained by one inserted token: F ≤ 0.3 (equivalently d_also ≥ 3.03); this rules out any single inserted word as the explanation, but not other meaning-changing words.
labels.undecided: The manipulation check fails: the “is also” own-format term is below 7.3 or the “is not” own-format term is more than 1.2 below 8.53.
